req.title: Redirect to arbitrary URL
req.statement: The system shall issue an HTTP 302 redirect to the URL given by the 'url' query parameter of /redirect-to.

doc.reasoning: The redirect_to() handler reads 'url' from query args, sets status_code=302 by default, and writes the exact URL string into the Location header. To maximise mutation kill rate I need to: (1) assert status_code == 302 exactly (catches 301/303 mutations); (2) assert Location == the exact supplied URL string (catches any mangling); (3) test the status_code override path at the boundary values 299, 300, 399, 400 (catches off-by-one on the 300<=sc<400 guard); (4) test missing 'url' param (negative path, KeyError/500); (5) test a URL with special characters to verify UTF-8 pass-through; (6) test that a status_code outside the redirect range is ignored and 302 is returned.

tests.name: test_redirect_to_basic_302_and_exact_location
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
GET /redirect-to?url=<target> is reachable via test client
trace: R-HTTPBIN-024: status 302 and Location set to supplied url
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_redirect_to_basic_302_and_exact_location():
    r = client.get('/redirect-to?url=https://example.com')
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.headers['Location'] == 'https://example.com'

test_redirect_to_basic_302_and_exact_location()

tests.name: test_redirect_to_location_matches_supplied_url_exactly

tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_redirect_to_location_matches_supplied_url_exactly():
    target = 'http://httpbin.org/get'
    r = client.get('/redirect-to?url=' + target)
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.headers['Location'] == target
